title: Postage drawer: Proof strip
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: For each nonnegative postage amount, produce the smallest number of stamps needed using unlimited denominations 1, 4 and 9. Zero postage uses zero stamps. Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.
descriptionMd:
An old postage drawer contains unlimited stamps valued at one, four and nine units. Luz rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

For each nonnegative postage amount, produce the smallest number of stamps needed using unlimited denominations 1, 4 and 9. Zero postage uses zero stamps.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement postageDrawerProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Unbounded dynamic programming. For each nonnegative postage amount, produce the smallest number of stamps needed using unlimited denominations 1, 4 and 9. Zero postage uses zero stamps. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n + M); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with unbounded dynamic programming. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each nonnegative postage amount, produce the smallest number of stamps needed using unlimited denominations 1, 4 and 9. Zero postage uses zero stamps. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
